([[Lafayette, Indiana]]) | college = [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] (2021–present) | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2024]]) * Big Ten All-Defensive Team (2024) * Honorable mention All-[[Big Ten Conference]] (2025) * Big Ten Sportsmanship Award (2025) | draft_year = 2025 }} '''Brooks Barnhizer''' (born March 2, 2002){{Cite web |title=Brooks Barnhizer Player Profile, Northwestern - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Brooks-Barnhizer/Summary/162075 |access-date=2025-05-04 |website=basketball.realgm.com |language=en}} is an American [[college basketball]] player for [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. In May 2025, Barnhizer was invited to the [[NBA G League Elite Camp]], a pre‑draft showcase for NBA prospects.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/2025-g-league-elite-camp|title=NBA G League Invites 45 Prospects to 2025 Elite Camp|publisher=NBA.com|date=May 6, 2025|access-date=May 6, 2025}} ==Early life and high school== Barnhizer grew up in [[South Bend, Indiana]] before moving to [[Irvington, Alabama]] in 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/family-affair-indiana-native-mark-barnhizer-2-sons-putting-alma-bryant-basketball-on-map/|title='Family affair:' Indiana native Mark Barnhizer, 2 sons putting Alma Bryant basketball on map|website=[[AL.com]]|date=January 11, 2018|access-date=November 6, 2024}} He began playing for the varsity basketball team at [[Alma Bryant High School]], where his father was the head basketball coach, while in eight grade.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/01/23/indiana-high-school-basketball-brooks-barnhizer-lafayette-jeff-mr-basketball-northwestern-commit/6660750002/|title=State's leading scorer Brooks Barnhizer having monster season. 'He does this every night.'|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=January 23, 2021|access-date=November 6, 2024}} After his sophomore year, Barnhizer's family moved to [[Lafayette, Indiana]] and he transferred to [[Jefferson High School (Indiana)|Jefferson High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/high-school/2023/03/31/fau-coach-got-foundation-of-basketball-from-laf-jeffs-barnhizer/70065618007/|title=FAU's Dusty May got 'foundation of basketball' from Lafayette Jeff's Mark Barnhizer|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2024}} He averaged 20.7 points per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/01/28/indiana-mr-basketball-2021-candidates-trey-kaufman-caleb-furst-luke-brown-brooks-barnhizer/6699549002/|title=2021 Indiana Mr. Basketball: These 12 players have strong cases|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=November 6, 2024}} As a senior, Barnhizer averaged a state-high 32.7 points per game while also averaging 11.5 rebounds, 6.5 assists, 3.8 steals, and 2.6 blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2021/04/24/j-c-big-school-player-year-lafayette-jeffs-brooks-barnhizer/7290317002/|title=J&C Big School Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Lafayette Jeff's Brooks Barnhizer|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=April 24, 2021|access-date=November 6, 2024}} Barnhizer was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] over offers from [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], and [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2020/06/21/lafayette-jeffs-brooks-barnhizer-commits-northwestern-basketball/3233747001/|title=Lafayette Jeff's Brooks Barnhizer commits to Northwestern basketball|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=June 21, 2020|access-date=November 6, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/06/21/brooks-barnhizer-a-top-150-basketball-recruit-from-indiana-commits-to-northwesterns-2021-class/|title=Brooks Barnhizer, a top-150 basketball recruit from Indiana, commits to Northwestern's 2021 class|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=June 21, 2020|access-date=November 6, 2024}} ==College career== Barnhizer played in 11 games during his freshman season with the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]] and averaged 1.7 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/basketball/big-ten-basketball-breakout-players-2023-24-season|title=Big Ten Basketball Breakout Players For 2023-24 Season|first=Jack|last=Ankony|website=SI.com|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2024}} He played in all 34 of the Wildcats’ games as a sophomore as the team’s sixth man and averaged 7.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/high-school/2023/03/14/brooks-barnhizer-lifting-ncaa-tournament-bound-northwestern/69999726007/|title=Brooks Barnhizer lifting NCAA tournament bound Northwestern|work=Journal & Courier|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.insidenu.com/2024/6/8/24174288/what-would-brooks-barnhizer-look-like-running-the-point-for-nu|title=What would Brooks Barnhizer look like running the point for NU?|first=Ryan|last=Cole|website=InsideNU.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=June 8, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2024}} ===Junior Season (2023–24)=== During his junior season, Barnhizer moved into Northwestern’s starting lineup and started all 34 games, averaging 14.6 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.8 steals, and 0.8 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.insidenu.com/2024/10/30/24281714/2024-25-mens-basketball-player-previews-brooks-barnhizer|title=2024-25 Men’s Basketball Player Previews: Brooks Barnhizer|first=Charlie|last=Jacobs|website=InsideNU.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=October 30, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2024}} He recorded 10 double-doubles—the most in a single season by a Northwestern guard—and was named third-team All-[[Big Ten Conference]] as well as earning a spot on the Big Ten All-Defensive Team.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2024/11/02/northwestern-basketball-big-ten-preview/|title=Can Northwestern basketball finish with a winning record in 3 straight seasons for the 1st time since 2012?|work=Chicago Tribune|date=November 2, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2024}} He also played a key role in Northwestern’s consecutive NCAA Tournament appearances, including scoring the tying layup to force overtime in the Wildcats’ first-round win over Florida Atlantic. ===Senior Season (2024–25)=== In his senior season, Barnhizer was selected to the preseason All-[[Big Ten Conference]] team by media. Through 17 games, he averaged 17.1 points, 8.8 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 2.3 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game, recording nine double-doubles with a streak of seven consecutive games—a program record.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/2025/01/20/northwestern-basketball-barnhizer-senior-season-update|title=Northwestern's Barnhizer making impact in senior season before injury|work=Journal & Courier|date=January 20, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2024}} In January 2025, he aggravated a lingering foot injury and missed the remainder of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/2025/01/15/northwestern-basketball-barnhizer-foot-injury|title=Northwestern's Barnhizer sidelined with foot injury|work=Journal & Courier|date=January 15, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2024}} Despite the shortened campaign, he earned honorable mention All-[[Big Ten Conference]] honors and was recognized as Northwestern’s Big Ten Sportsmanship Award honoree. ===Career Statistics and Milestones=== Barnhizer finished his collegiate career with 1,067 points, posting career averages of 11.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists over 96 games (51 starts). He became the first Big Ten player since Michael Redd to reach at least 1,000 points, 500 rebounds, and 200 assists within his first 96 career games, while also recording 133 steals and 62 blocks.{{cite web|url=https://www.insidenu.com/2024/10/30/24281714/2024-25-mens-basketball-player-previews-brooks-barnhizer|title=2024-25 Men’s Basketball Player Previews: Brooks Barnhizer|first=Charlie|last=Jacobs|website=InsideNU.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=October 30, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2024}} ==Pre‑draft process== On May 6, 2025, Barnhizer was one of 45 prospects invited to the 2025 [[NBA G League Elite Camp]] at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, scheduled for May 9–11. The event gives participants a chance to earn selection to the NBA Draft Combine based on their performance.{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/college/northwestern/alumni/former-northwestern-basketball-star-heading-g-league-elite-camp |title=Former Northwestern Star Brooks Barnhizer Heading to G League Elite Camp |work=Sports Illustrated |date=May 6, 2025 |access-date=May 6, 2025}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://nusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brooks-barnhizer/11661 Northwestern Wildcats bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Barnhizer, Brooks}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indiana]] [[Category:Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Year of birth missing (living people)]]
